evidence.note: CreateBucket returned NoSuchBucket; agent diagnosed that its cross-tenant existence check was wrongly applied to CreateBucket and revised the dispatch logic to bypass it — a design-level fix of the actual cause, not a symptom patch.

Multipart complete failed with InvalidPart; agent traced it to XML namespace handling and recognized it as a CLASS of failure, propagating a _strip_ns fix across ALL parsers (complete, delete, tagging, CORS, lifecycle, notification) rather than patching one — correction propagated through affected subsystems.

Unicode-key SigV4 failure: agent deeply diagnosed a foundational signing/path-encoding assumption (wsgiref latin-1 decode vs boto3 canonical URI encoding), verified signatures matched in isolation, discovered the patch hadn't actually applied, and corrected the WSGI path decoding — a foundational-assumption revision.
After the SigV4/encoding fix, re-ran the full battery (test1/test2/test4/test5) to confirm no dependents regressed — re-verification of dependents after a design change.

reasoning: The agent repeatedly treated verification failures as signal about the design: it revised the cross-tenant/CreateBucket dispatch, fixed a foundational SigV4 path-encoding assumption falsified by boto3, and re-verified dependents afterward, matching the level-8 anchor. Notably it recognized the XML-namespace failure as a class and propagated the fix across all parsers, and confirmed fixes with targeted re-runs — behaviors toward the top of the scale. It falls short of 10 because corrections were reactive to test failures rather than proactive structural de-risking, and no large-altitude pivot (e.g., storage/concurrency model) was needed or made.
